title: 10 Simple Tweaks For Instant Behavior Improvement ovement/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin offers ten small, immediately usable adjustments teachers can make to see quick behavioral gains, framed around his premise that classroom management is a learnable, knowledge-based skill. The tweaks range from deciding in advance to stay calm and slowing down one's pace, to talking less, reviewing the classroom management plan briefly, and previewing upcoming lessons to build anticipation. He also emphasizes resting in the freedom that a consistently enforced plan provides, rather than trying to control behavior through willpower or coercion. The piece closes by noting these are only a starting point among hundreds of strategies in the site's archive.
points: Deciding in advance to maintain a calm demeanor before the day starts is framed as foundational to eliminating excitability.
Cutting talking time by roughly a third and being more specific improves how well students listen and follow directions.
A brief, non-repetitive review of the classroom management plan keeps its importance present without belaboring it.
Previewing and 'selling' the day's most compelling lessons gives students a motive to attend and behave.
Relying solely on the classroom management plan frees the teacher from needing to raise their voice or coerce compliance.
quotes: If you’re a longtime reader of Smart Classroom Management, then you know that we hold true the belief that classroom management is knowledge based.
Before your students arrive for the day, make a decision to keep a calm demeanor throughout.
If you can cut the amount of talking you do by a third, you’ll notice a substantial difference in how well your students listen, attend, and follow your directions.
Think of the most compelling topics and activities you plan to teach that day and sell them to your students.
Relying solely on your classroom management plan frees you to enjoy being a teacher.
